examples.japanese: {風速|ふうそく}{30|さんじゅう}メートルの{強風|きょうふう}だ。
examples.english: It's a strong wind with a speed of 30 meters per second.

examples.japanese: {最大|さいだい}{瞬間|しゅんかん}{風速|ふうそく}を{記録|きろく}した。
examples.english: The maximum instantaneous wind speed was recorded.

examples.japanese: {台風|たいふう}の{接近|せっきん}で{風速|ふうそく}が{急激|きゅうげき}に{上|あ}がり、{外出|がいしゅつ}が{危険|きけん}になった。
examples.english: With the typhoon approaching, the wind speed rose sharply and going outside became dangerous.

notes:
Compound of {風|ふう} (wind) and {速|そく} (speed). Frequently heard in weather reports and typhoon coverage. In Japan, wind speed is measured in meters per second (m/s), unlike some countries that use kilometers per hour.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {最大|さいだい}{風速|ふうそく}: maximum wind speed
- {最大|さいだい}{瞬間|しゅんかん}{風速|ふうそく}: maximum instantaneous wind speed
- {平均|へいきん}{風速|ふうそく}: average wind speed
- {風速|ふうそく}〜メートル: wind speed of ~ meters per second
- {風速|ふうそく}{計|けい}: anemometer

WEATHER CONTEXT:
Japanese weather reports classify wind strength by {風速|ふうそく}:
- {強風|きょうふう}: strong wind (15 m/s or more)
- {暴風|ぼうふう}: violent wind (25 m/s or more)
- {猛烈|もうれつ}な{風|かぜ}: extreme wind (35 m/s or more)
